raw_case_text: A 4-month-old HIV-exposed female infant presented to the emergency department with multifocal convulsion, dystonic posturing, and altered sensorium. She was born at 35-36 weeks of gestation by emergency cesarean section due to cord prolapse. The mother was diagnosed to be HIV infected before pregnancy and was on ART consisting of AZT, lamivudine (3TC), and nevirapine (NVP), which she continued till date. Her CD4 count was 560 cells/mm3 at the time of delivery. The baby also received single-dose NPV after birth and then AZT prophylaxis for 6 weeks. The child was exclusively breastfed. At presentation, the child had pallor, altered sensorium, and dystonic posturing. Anterior fontanel was at level and reflexes were brisk though tone was normal, and there was no focal neurological deficit. She had acidotic breathing with hepatomegaly. Other systemic examination was normal. Complete blood count was normal except hypochromic, microcytic anemia (hemoglobin was 9 g/dl). Liver and renal functions were normal, but arterial blood gas analysis showed severe metabolic acidosis (pH: 7.14, bicarbonate: 4.2 mEq/L) with a high anion gap of 30. Serum electrolytes were as follows: sodium: 138 mEq/L and potassium: 4.3 mEq/L. Septic screen in the form of C-reactive protein and blood culture was negative. Plasma sugar was 256 mg/dl, and urine was negative for ketones. The child was treated with intravenous fluids and anticonvulsants. Her sensorium gradually improved. Computed tomography brain revealed bilateral basal ganglia hypodensities suggestive of metabolic encephalopathy [Figure 1]. Serum lactate levels were sent after 24 h of hospitalization and after correction of acidosis which was normal (14 mEq/L [normal: 12-22]). Subsequent blood sugars were normal. Serum ammonia was 70 mmol/L (normal: 30-90 mmol/L), and urinary organic acids screen was normal. Electroencephalogram revealed generalized slowing. Mother was advised to stop breastfeeds and start replacement feeds. Child's HIV polymerase chain reaction was negative. The patient was put on thiamine, biotin, carnitine, and coenzyme Q supplements and regular physiotherapy. She is on regular follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 4-month-old HIV-exposed female infant presented to the emergency department with multifocal convulsions, dystonic posturing, and altered sensorium.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Born at 35–36 weeks' gestation via emergency cesarean section for umbilical cord prolapse to an HIV-infected mother on continuous zidovudine, lamivudine, and nevirapine (maternal delivery CD4 count 560 cells/mm3), the infant received single-dose nevirapine at birth and 6 weeks of zidovudine prophylaxis while being exclusively breastfed, before presenting acutely at 4 months of age with multifocal seizures, dystonia, Kussmaul/acidotic breathing, and encephalopathy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Perinatal antiretroviral exposure (maternal AZT/3TC/NVP throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding, plus neonatal single-dose NVP and 6-week AZT prophylaxis); born late preterm (35–36 weeks) via emergency C-section for cord prolapse.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for multifocal seizures, dystonic posturing, altered consciousness, and rapid/deep acidotic breathing.

objective.physical_examination: Pale infant with altered sensorium, multifocal convulsions, dystonic posturing, Kussmaul (acidotic) breathing, and hepatomegaly. Anterior fontanelle was normotensive (at level), deep tendon reflexes were brisk with normal muscle tone, and no focal lateralizing neurological deficits were present.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC showed microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL) with normal leukocyte and platelet counts. Liver and renal function tests, serum electrolytes (sodium 138 mEq/L, potassium 4.3 mEq/L), serum ammonia (70 µmol/L; normal 30–90 µmol/L), and urine organic acid screen were normal. Arterial blood gas demonstrated severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis (pH 7.14, bicarbonate 4.2 mEq/L, anion gap 30); admission blood glucose was 256 mg/dL with negative urine ketones (subsequent blood sugars normal), and post-resuscitation serum lactate at 24 hours was normal (14 mEq/L; normal 12–22). CRP and blood cultures were negative; infant HIV DNA/RNA PCR was negative. EEG showed generalized background slowing.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast head CT demonstrated symmetric bilateral basal ganglia hypodensities consistent with mitochondrial/metabolic encephalopathy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Zidovudine/nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI)-induced mitochondrial toxicity presenting as severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis (pH 7.14, HCO3- 4.2 mEq/L, anion gap 30) and bilateral basal ganglia metabolic encephalopathy in an HIV-exposed, uninfected 4-month-old female infant (infant HIV PCR negative; exposed in utero, via 6-week neonatal AZT prophylaxis, and via ongoing breastmilk to maternal AZT/3TC/NVP). Managed with intravenous fluid/bicarbonate resuscitation, anticonvulsants, immediate cessation of breastfeeding (transitioned to formula replacement feeding to halt ongoing maternal NRTI exposure), a mitochondrial cofactor cocktail (thiamine, biotin, L-carnitine, and coenzyme Q10), and regular physical therapy, resulting in sensorium recovery and stable outpatient follow-up.
